fault_type: Slow upstream drift propagating to a downstream measurement

steps.statement: The incoming data passed all quality checks, so what follows is about the process, not the instruments.
Starting around sample 320, the combined behaviour of the signals moved away from normal operation by more than twice the usual amount.
Almost half of that movement comes from one signal that has been climbing steadily without ever leaving its normal range, which is why no simple alarm fired.
A second signal follows it with the same delay it shows during normal operation, so the two are still physically linked and the first one is driving.

ranked_sensors.why: Largest single contribution to the deviation, and it leads the others in time.
Moves after col_031 with the delay established during normal operation.

alternatives_considered.hypothesis: A drifting instrument on col_031 rather than a real process change
alternatives_considered.why_rejected: Correlated neighbours moved consistently; a calibration drift on one instrument would not propagate with the expected lag.
alternatives_considered.residual_doubt: A slow drift in a shared reference would look the same. Not ruled out.

critique.adjustment_reason: The shared-reference alternative could not be excluded from the available signals.

uncertainties: The physical unit of col_031 is unknown; the role is inferred from behaviour only.
The baseline covers normal operation only; seasonal or load-dependent variation is not represented.
